items.stem: What is the minimum you should log to make a training run reproducible?

options.text: Parameters, code/data versions, environment and the resulting metrics
options.rationale: Correct: reproducibility needs the full context, not just the score.
A number alone cannot reproduce the run.
The artifact without params/versions cannot be reproduced.
Insufficient; versions and params are also required.

items.stem: A model has been logged dozens of times. Which TWO things does a model registry add beyond a pile of logged artifacts? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Named stages/aliases such as staging and production
options.rationale: Correct: a registry governs which version is in which stage.

options.text: An auditable promotion and approval workflow
options.rationale: Correct: registries record who promoted what and when.

options.text: Faster GPU training of the model
options.rationale: Registries do not change training speed.

options.text: Automatic relabelling of the training data

items.explanation: Correct: a registry governs which version is in which stage.

items.stem: A new model version scores slightly higher offline. Why is promoting it to production automatically risky?

options.text: Offline gains may not hold online and there is no approval or rollback plan
options.rationale: Correct: promotion should pass a gate with online checks and a rollback path.

options.text: Higher offline scores always transfer to production
options.rationale: They often do not, due to distribution shift and metric mismatch.

options.text: Registries forbid having more than one version
options.rationale: Registries are designed to hold many versions.

options.text: The older version cannot be kept

items.explanation: Correct: promotion should pass a gate with online checks and a rollback path.
